sources.note: Uses elliptical bonuses over a language model's own hidden-state representations as a diversity signal, validates it in a clean inference-time selection setting, then transfers the same signal into RL post-training — where it eliminates the diversity collapse that degrades pass@k at large k.
sources.title: Representation-Based Exploration for Language Models: From Test-Time to Post-Training

sources.note: Tracks mutual information between each reasoning step's representation and the correct answer, finds it spikes at sparse 'MI peaks' that decode to reflective tokens like 'Wait' and 'Hmm', and shows suppressing exactly those tokens degrades reasoning while suppressing equally many others does not.
sources.title: Demystifying Reasoning Dynamics with Mutual Information: Thinking Tokens are Information Peaks in LLM Reasoning

sources.note: Establishes that RL trades policy entropy for reward along a predictable exponential curve R = -a·exp(H) + b, derives that entropy change is driven by the covariance between action probability and advantage, and controls it by restricting updates to the highest-covariance tokens.
sources.title: The Entropy Mechanism of Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

sources.note: Measures RLVR-trained models against their base models with pass@k at large k and finds the base wins, concluding RLVR sharpens sampling toward paths the base already had rather than adding new ones.
sources.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

sources.note: Converts AMC23 and AIME24/25 into symbolic templates whose constants are replaced by sampled variables, requires a model to solve several instantiations of each problem, and finds RL-finetuned models lose most of their reported accuracy under that consistency requirement.
sources.title: VAR-MATH: Probing True Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs via Symbolic Multi-Instance Benchmarks

sources.note: Proves that an entropy bonus permanently moves the stationary point of RL training while covariance-targeted control reaches the unregularized optimum once its coefficient is annealed, and that the bonus shrinks the stability margin where the targeted methods leave it intact.
sources.title: A Comparative Theoretical Analysis of Entropy Control Methods in Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

sources.note: Shows that base models win pass@K on mathematics by producing wrong chains that land on right answers, and that scoring the chain too — CoT-Pass@K — reverses the verdict in RLVR's favour at every K.
sources.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs

result.definition: The 32B base model of the Qwen2.5 family, used across these sources as the large end of RLVR experiments. It is where covariance-targeted entropy control shows its biggest margins — 6.4 points average over GRPO against 2.0 at 7B, with 15.0 and 14.6 points on AIME24 and AIME25 — a scale trend several sources report and one theoretical entry reads as larger models holding more latent capacity that sustained exploration can unlock. It is also among the models whose scores collapse under symbolic variation, falling from 33.4 to 3.1 on a variabilized AMC23, and it appears in the pass@k comparisons where base models overtake their RLVR-trained counterparts once k grows into the hundreds.
